text:
maria: Quick q — if we unpin a model variant for /generate what guarantees do clients have? Will requests automatically fall back to a compatible model or return an error? Need exact wording for deprecation docs.
jon: We currently do a family-level fallback for hosted: runtime picks the best compatible model. If nothing compatible, we return 409 with a tiny JSON explanation. Not always ideal but predictable.
lee: We also support header negotiation. Runtime checks Accept-Model or X-Model-Version before fallback. Example: 
```bash
curl -H "Accept-Model: redwood-llm/2.1" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
If no match it moves down the fallback chain then 409.
oliver: Note: Dedicated/Private are strict by default (pin = single model). You can opt in to auto-fallback with a deployment flag. Example: 
```yaml
deployment:
  model_pin: redwood-llm/2.1
  enable_auto_fallback: true
```
maria: OK. For comms — propose deprecation timeline: 14d warning header + 7d hard-deprecate (21d total) and a console banner. Thoughts?
jon: 21d is tight for some enterprise customers. Suggest Hosted = 14d, Dedicated/Private = 30d.
lee: +1 to differentiating by deployment type. Hosted 14d, Dedicated/Private 30d, with ability to extend per-customer.
oliver: I'll open a docs PR with Accept-Model examples, config snippets, and migration steps.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: patch-runtime/fallback-checks v1.2 deployed to staging :white_check_mark:
maria: Awesome. Action items: @oliver file the docs PR, @lee add header negotiation notes to runtime README, @jon wire TTLs into the deprecation service (14/30). I'll draft the external deprecation comms once those land. :eyes:
